doc.title: Joe Wilder Part 1 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996

title: Joining Basie and the note asking for a solo
summary: Joe Newman asked for help carrying solos so Wilder joined Basie; he wrote Basie a note asking to play and was told to go ahead.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: How did the gig with Basie come about? It’s usually word of mouth, isn’t it, that leads somewhere?

Well I knew Basie and I knew a lot of people in the band. But Joe Newman was the featured trumpet soloist basically. He played most of the trumpet solos, not all of them, but he was working so much and he said that they needed to get someone else to take some of the load off of him. And Basie was looking for someone and that’s how I came to join the band. And it was actually, to take a little of the pressure off Joe.
Did you get a lot of his solos?
Did you get a lot of his solos?

I did some, yes, I had some too. Yeah. It was interesting you know, it was interesting. I was telling that story this morning, about after having joined the band I was there a couple of weeks, a few weeks, and I hadn’t played any solos. And I was getting a little frustrated. So I wrote a little note to Count Basie and I said “Bas, could I play a couple of choruses of just about anything?” And I signed it “the trumpet player second from the drums.” You know Joe sat here, I sat here and the drums are there. And I passed the note over to Basie, and Basie took it, and he stopped playing and he looked at it and he said “you want to play, go ahead and play.” And you know he was very nice you know.
